links.reason: Both have birds at a warrior's body (288 மொய்த்தன பருந்தே; 291 இரும்புள் பூசல் ஓம்புமின்), a stock battlefield picture. Calling 291's guarding 'the answer to 288's loss' builds a dialogue between two unrelated poems; 288's would-be embracer sits in a lost line.

The wording is nearly the same: 307 பொதியிற் கடவுள் போகிய கருந்தாட் கந்தத்து and 52 கடவுள் கந்தம் கைவிடப் ... பாழ்படு பொதியில், and in both a bird lives in the ruin. 307 turns it with உடனுறை பழமையின் துறத்தல் செல்லாது, a dove that will not leave where the god left, set against the hero leaving (நீங்கல் ஒல்லுமோ).

216 கேட்டல் மாத்திரை அல்லது ... காண்டல் இல்லாது ... கிழமையர் and Kural 785 புணர்ச்சி பழகுதல் வேண்டா ... நட்பாங் கிழமை தரும் make the same claim with the same technical word. 216 applies it as a wager (ஒழிக்க அவற்கு இடமே), so 'develops' fits.

233 laments the report of wounds on Evvi, இரும்பாண் ஒக்கல் தலைவன், and 115 recalls எவ்வி வீழ்ந்த செருவில் பாணர் breaking their yazh necks, which it uses as a simile for konrai pods. The note says what the akam poet does with the name, and the bards' grief links the two sides.

The shared words are real (கிழமைத் தொன்னட்பு against பழைமை ... கிழமை), but 223's கிழமை is closeness like life's love for the body, while 801's is a friend's claim or liberty. The teaches reads the friends' going to the stone as a liberty the king tolerates, which takes the liberty sense from commentary rather than from 223.
links.text_issue: 223 line 2 (தலைப்போ கன்மையிற் சிறுவழி மடங்கி) is compressed and unclear.

links.reason: 55 has ஞாயிற் றன்ன வெந்திறல் ... திங்கள் அன்ன தண்பெருஞ் சாயலும as qualities the king should hold (உடையை ஆகி ... வாழிய), and 59 has ஞாயிறு அனையை நின் பகைவர்க்கு; திங்கள் அனையை எம்மனோர்க்கே. The note is accurate: the second names whom each face is turned to.

Both returning heroes urge the charioteer past a male beast with its mate (64 மடநாகு தழீஇ, 34 மடப்பிணை அருத்தி), the shared convention of the thurai. Nothing shows that 64, by another poet, extends 34. The bells (ஆபூண் தெண்மணி ... கேட்டொறும் கலங்கினள்) belong to 64 alone, so the pair teaches only the shared convention.

52 has no spear or lightning; its image is the tiger leaving its cave. The only tie is the colophon poet and the common Pandya name வழுதி (312 வெல்போர் வழுதி; 52's patron is the Kudakaratthu Maran Vazhuthi). That is a shared name and attribution dressed up as a shared image.

Both are about mortality. 356's burning ground எல்லார் புறனும் தான்கண்டு is a vivid place, but making it the 'greatness' that Kural 336's பெருமை names is an equation the couplet does not support: there பெருமை is the world's quality of transience, not a survivor. The pairing rests on the shared topic of death.

The verbal match is close: 112 சான்றோர் பழியொடு வரூஉம் இன்பம் வெஃகார், and Kural 657 பழிமலைந்து எய்திய ஆக்கத்தின் சான்றோர் கழிநல் குரவே தலை. The Kural's rule leaves only privation, while the friend adds a way out, marriage (வரையின் எவனோ), which removes the blame and keeps the pleasure. That is a real qualification.

Same poet and patron. 381 promises (இலம்பாடு அகற்றல்) and 384 says the chief kept giving (யான் தண்டவும், தான் தண்டான்). That turning 381's sign (இதற்கொண்டு அறிநை) into 384's uncounted days (வந்த வைகல் அல்லது) is a constructed bridge, and the 'loss' rests on the colophon's கையறுநிலை, which the poem does not state.
links.text_issue: 384 has gaps at lines 5, 10 and 13; 381's quotation marks are unbalanced.

links.reason: Both are Paranar's under the thurai அல்ல குறி. Both measure the girl by the Velir treasure at Pazhi (372 அருங்கல வெறுக்கையின் அரியோள், 258 பொன்னினும் அருமை) and both turn on எனினும் அஃது ஒல்லாய். The endings differ as the teaches says: 258 மாய்கதில், 372 the swing, drum-strap and snake similes.

The fruiting tree as an image of giving is common: 199's god's banyan with birds returning (நெருநல் உண்டனம் என்னாது) and Kural 216's பயன்மரம் உள்ளூர்ப் பழுத்தற்று. 199's point is that the giver's wealth is the asker's wealth (உடைமை ஆகும், அவர் உடைமை), not that the asker's return is a sign of the giver's worth, so the teaches overreads it.

Kural 737 lists a country's உறுப்பு; 187 says goodness lies in its men (எவ்வழி நல்லவர் ஆடவர் அவ்வழி நல்லை). These answer different questions, so 187 at most qualifies the material list. The teaches' claim that the Purananuru gave its answer 'before' the treatise is chronology the verses do not give.

101's பொய்யா காதே, of Athiyaman's gift, matches 162's நசைபிழைப்பு அறியாக் கழல்தொடி அதிகன், a real tie by name. The note does not say what Paranar does with Athikan: his hill frames the goddess simile for the girl. 'Fixed epithet' is more than a single line can show.

204 addresses ஓரி as a giver like the rain cloud (வரையாது சுரக்கும் வள்ளியோய்), and 209 recalls வல்வில் ஓரிக் கொன்று சேரலர்க்கு ஈத்த Kolli of Kari. One man appears as a living patron and as a victim in another chief's fame, which neither poem shows alone.

246 measures gossip by the roar for Karikal at வெண்ணி வாயில், when பதினொரு வேளிரொடு வேந்தர் சாய. 66 sets the defeated king who புறப்புண் நாணி, வடக்கிருந்தோனே above the victor. The same battle serves as a measure of noise and as a lesson in honour, as the teaches says.

In 216, செல்லிக் கோமான் ... வெள்வேல் ஆதன் எழினி அருநிறத்து அழுத்திய பெருங்களிற்று எவ்வம் most naturally makes Aathan Ezhini the lord of Chelli whose spear struck a great tusker's chest. He is not the one wounded. The note and teaches build on him being speared, which the marker itself flagged as uncertain. If the two do name the same chief, 216 remembers him as a striker, not 'only for his death wound'.

The rite is the same: 131 பெயரும் பீடும் எழுதி ... பீலி சூட்டிய பிறங்குநிலை நடுகல், and 264 அணிமயிற் பீலி சூட்டிப், பெயர்பொறித்து ... கல்லும், both for men of the cattle fights. 264 measures one loss through the bards' troupe, while 131 lines the road with such stones as the reason for வாரேன்.

Both picture the widow's austerities (280 சிறுவெள் ஆம்பல் அல்லி உண்ணும் கழிகல மகளிர், 246 the list ending பரற்பெய் பள்ளி). But 280's அதனினும் அரிதே compares that life with the bards' hard lot (நுமக்கும் ... அரிதே), not with death. 'Only a queen could choose against them' is in neither poem.

The image is distinctive and the same: 190 கேழல் இடம்பட வீழ்ந்தென, அன்று அவண் உண்ணாது, and Naladiyar 300 இடம்வீழ்ந்தது உண்ணாது இறக்கும். The Naladiyar applies it to one's own honour (மானம் மழுங்க வரின்), while 190 applies it to choosing friends (உரனுடையாளர் கேண்மை), as the teaches says.

Both are Paranar's on Aay Eyinan falling to Minjili, a real shared legend. 148's owl only 'did not go to see' (காணிய செல்லாக் கூகை நாணி). Making it a second bird left out of 208's shading (புள்ஒருங்கு ... நிழல்செய்து) is a reconstruction; in 208 the shading is in speech tied to Nannan's refusal to see the field, which is itself uncertain.
links.text_issue: 208 lines 12 to 18 (Nannan and அகுதை கிளைதந்தாங்கு) are obscure.

links.reason: Both name hunger a disease: 173 பசிப்பிணி மருத்துவன், Kural 227 பசியென்னும் தீப்பிணி. The Kural promises the sharer immunity (தீண்டல் அரிது), while 173 makes the giver the physician of others, a specific shift the pair shows.

236 ஒருங்குவரல் விடாஅது ‘ஒழிக’ எனக்கூறி and 222 என்இவண் ஒழித்த அன்பிலாள voice one grievance in one verb: the patron kept his friend from following. Kapilar resolves it by asking உயர்ந்த பால் for the next birth, while Pothiyar asks என்னிடம் யாது.

The blame word is shared (336 அறன்இலன் ... பண்புஇல் தாயே, 60 அறன்இல் யாயே), and the teaches rightly contrasts guarding the girl in akam with rearing a beauty that breeds war (பகைவளர்த்து) in the magatpar kaanchi. That is the same charge in two domains, not one poem extending the other.

Both refuse விழுப்பொருள் for a woman, and both name Muziri's gold and pepper trade. But in 149, Muziri sits in the chain about Chezhiyan's conquest leading to Koodal and the hill pool; it is not the measure of the wealth refused (அரிதுசெய் விழுப்பொருள் எளிதினிற் பெறினும்). So 'stock measure' overstates 149.

The formula உறந்தைக் குணாது is the same in both, but it only locates a hill and a town. That akam geography uses the real map is general and true of many poems; the pair shows nothing more than a shared place phrase.

Both show the waterless bandit road, a stock paalai scene: 313 வம்பலர் கணையிடத் தொலைந்தோர் ... குருதி மாந்தி with crows, and 3 அம்புவிட, வீழ்ந்தோர் வம்பப் பதுக்கை with kites. Setting the suppliant beside the husband who crosses for gain (பொருள்புரிந்து) is apt but thin.

There is no incompatible claim: one queen refuses the widow's life (உயவற் பெண்டிரேம் அல்லேம்) and another widow lives it, which are different situations. The note's 'greens and alli' puts 248's (or 280's) alli into 246, which names வேளை and பிண்டம். 248 does not present her austerity as a choice.

Both are Kayamanar's mothers after an elopement. In 189 the loss widens to the town (ஊர்இழந் தன்று, தன் வீழ்வுஉறு பொருளே). In 195 the mother concedes அருளான் ஆயினும், notes the other mother's joyful preparations and asks the velan எம்மனை முந்துறத் தருமோ, so the pair shows grief turning toward the homecoming.

Both name Tittan: 6 மழைவளம் தரூஉம் மாவண் தித்தன், and 80 நல்கினும் நல்கான் ஆயினும் ... தித்தன் காண்கதில். That is a real tie by name. But the note does not say what the akam poet does with Tittan (Uranthai as the scene of the Kaveri bath), and 'withholding judge' takes a single concessive clause further than it goes.

Kural 230 சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை இனிததூஉம் ஈதல் இயையாக் கடை is acted out in 165: a bard leaving empty is நாடுஇழந் ததனினும் நனிஇன் னாது, and the giver offers his head (வாள்தந் தனனே, தலை எனக்கு ஈய). It is a precise heroic case of the maxim.

292 ties the warrior's breach of the toddy order (‘என்முறை வருக’ என்னான்) to holding the army, and 298 ties the dregs he is given to the king's not saying ‘நீ முந்து’. Both read drinking order as rank at the front, which the pair makes clear.
links.text_issue: Both poems are flagged uncertain; 298's poet name varies.

links.reason: Both are Kayamanar's foster mothers under the same thurai: 17 imagines the girl's சிலம்புஆர் சீறுடி on the waste, and 7 questions a doe and a hill girl on the road. The 'two stages' reading is fair, but it mostly restates the shared situation.

143 leaves the weeping woman unidentified (யார்கொல் அளியள்). In 144 she answers யாம், அவன் கிளைஞரேம் அல்லேம் and names the cause, எம்போல் ஒருத்தி நலன்நயந்து. The second poem gives voice and cause to what the first withheld, for the same patron.

The tie by name is real: Kari, and பெண்ணையம் in both (126 பெண்ணையம் படப்பை நாடு, 35 காரி ... பெண்ணையம் பேரியாற்று). But in 35 the river's fine ripples (நுண் அறல்) are a simile for the girl's hair, not the place of her flight, so the teaches misplaces it. The point about 126's phrase holds.

741 says a fort serves both attackers and those who அஞ்சித் தற்போற்றுபவர், and 775 counts a blink before a spear as flight for the வன்கணவர். These are different roles and situations, so there is no incompatible claim, and the teaches only restates that they differ.

Both put shame on the attacker, but the foe in 36 is not humbled: he sits at ease (ஆங்குஇனி திருந்த வேந்தன்). Naladiyar 241's shame is before பகைவர் பணிவிடம். The overlap is partial, and 'the poets used this to bring wars to an end' goes beyond 36's அடுநை யாயினும் விடுநை யாயினும்.

Same poet, and both name Chellur. In 220 the guarded sacrificial pillar (அருங்கடி நெடுந்தூண்) measures the girl's unapproachability. In 90 Chellur only locates the Kosar market that measures her price (கோசர் நியமம் ... பாசிலை விலை), not a guarded object, so the teaches does not hold for 90.

The shared Anni and Thithiyan punnai story is real (126 புன்னை வெஃகித் திதியனொடு பொருத அன்னி, 145 திதியன் ... துமியப் பண்ணிய புன்னை). But 145's curse falls on the foster mother's own hand (அஞ்ஞையை அலைத்த கையே), not on 'the man who took a daughter', so the teaches misdescribes 145.

The two verses fit exactly through குடி: 45 ஒருவீர் தோற்பினும், தோற்ப நும் குடியே, and 888 உட்பகை உற்ற குடி wearing itself away like gold under a file. 45 adds the outside gainers (நும்மோர் அன்ன வேந்தர்க்கு மெய்ம்மலி உவகை), as the teaches says.

The wording is nearly the same: 73 ஆற்றல் உடையோர் ஆற்றல் போற்றாது, and Kural 891 ஆற்றுவார் ஆற்றல் இகழாமை போற்றுவார் போற்றலுள் எல்லாம் தலை. The change of viewpoint, a vow from the strong against a warning to all, is accurate.

Both use the crossing (357 புணைகை விட்டோர்க்கு அரிதே ... உக்கரை கொளலே; Kural 10 பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர்). With line 6 lost, what the raft is cannot be read, so 'without a god' and the claim of priority do not hold.

iraicchi.act: the male wild dog attacks a boar because its mate, weak after giving birth, is hungry
iraicchi.sense: as the dog hunts for its mate, the man goes to win wealth for his household (மனைநகப் ... வெறுக்கை தருகம்)

ullurai.anchor: நெடுஞ்சுடர் விளக்கம் நோக்கி வந்து, நம் நடுங்குதுயர் களைந்த நன்னராளன்

poems.note: The hunter's torch is also the hero's literal guide, so the boar scene is partly setting as well as vehicle.

iraicchi.act: the male vulture hunts and kills to bring food to its mate weak after hatching
iraicchi.sense: it pictures the provider's pull that drives the heart to urge the man away for wealth, which he resists

iraicchi.act: the tusker holds its pregnant mate while their calf climbs on and off it, then they sleep
iraicchi.sense: seeing it on his road he will remember his wife and child and not delay (நீடலர்)

poems.note: The scene is openly likened to a family (மடவோள் தழீஇய விறலோன் மார்பில் ... ஆங்கு), which rules out ullurai but not iraicchi.
The heron is itself likened to a thief (கள்வன் போல), but that marker stays inside the vehicle and does not join it to the husband.
